title: Functions and closures — one screen
rememberThis: Function declarations hoist fully; const/let expressions do not — calling before the line throws ReferenceError.
Arrow functions capture lexical this and have no arguments object; regular functions get dynamic this from the call site.
Scope chain (where variables live) is not the call stack (which function runs now) — draw both in interviews.
Closures retain outer environments; for (var i) in a loop shares one binding — use let or an IIFE snapshot.
JavaScript has no reliable tail-call optimization in V8 — use loops or explicit stacks for unbounded recursion depth.
bullets: Default parameters trigger only when the argument is undefined, not null.
Rest parameters (...args) produce a real Array; arguments is legacy and absent in arrows.
IIFE + module pattern simulated privacy before ES modules — still common in legacy bundles.
Higher-order functions: map, debounce, once — all pass or return closures.
Long-lived event handlers that capture DOM nodes or large objects cause closure memory leaks.

rows.label: Declaration vs arrow
rows.value: Declaration hoists; arrow has lexical this, no new, no arguments.

rows.label: let vs var in loops
rows.value: let = per-iteration binding; var = one shared binding for all closures.

rows.label: Scope chain lookup
rows.value: Inner → outer → global. Fixed at definition time, not call time.

rows.label: Closure lifetime
rows.value: Outer env stays alive while any inner function referencing it is reachable.

rows.label: debounce / once
rows.value: HOF returns closure holding timer or called flag — standard interview builds.

rows.label: Stack overflow
rows.value: Sync recursion without base case → RangeError. Rewrite to iteration for production.
